solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Place false statement before head of university

parts.note: a lie is a statement known to be untrue

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of university is used

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a lie ahead of a university's principal, as if writing up some academic scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just orders the pieces: the lie comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu is a noun meaning stead or position, familiar from the phrase 'in lieu of'.

clue.text: Sake? This can make you most unsteady!

indicators.note: the letters of the two words can be rearranged to make something new, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: A warning that drinking Japanese rice wine will leave you wobbling worse than anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sake' and 'This' are rearranged as one pool of letters; 'you' only completes the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakiest is the superlative of shaky, so it means wobbling or trembling more than any other.

clue.text: Royal Artillery's turned up in dark to surrender weapons

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the word for dark

parts.note: dim means poorly lit, dark

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means these letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: RA is the abbreviation for the Royal Artillery, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Gunners turning up at night to hand over their arms, a military surrender scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives SAR, read upwards in this down light; 'in' looks like a link word but signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm is to give up or take away weapons, a verb matching the phrase.

clue.text: Supported — or retreated?

definitions.meaning: ... as in gave help or endorsement to someone
... as in moved backwards, as in '... away'

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone stood firm behind a cause or ran away.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb carries both senses: to back a cause is to support it, to back off is to withdraw.

clue.text: Live at home, outside evacuated regional capital

indicators.note: outside says the first pieces sit around the next one

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied of contents, leaving only the outer letters of regional

explanation.surface: Someone stays home while just outside the deserted regional capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' empties 'regional' to RL; BE and IN go 'outside' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is the capital city of Germany, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Price of firm's time

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A business question about what a company charges for its hours of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The cost of something is the amount paid for it, a synonym for its charge.

clue.text: Gems editor's penning lamer after revision

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen holding sheep, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: after revision means the word lamer has been reworked, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: An editor writes something even weaker after redrafting, with 'Gems' as the sardonic headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revision' gives MERAL; 'penning' reads like writing, but here it means enclosing, as a pen holds animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeralds are green precious stones, examples of gems.

clue.text: Greeting school quintet

parts.note: a high school is a secondary school, so high can stand for school
a quintet is a group of five

explanation.surface: A five-piece school band welcomes its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' gives HIGH only through 'high school', a loose but common crossword stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A high five is a celebratory slap of raised palms, used as a hello or congratulation.

clue.text: In Cyprus, settlers find apple

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the words that follow, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Colonists on Cyprus discover a fruit growing there.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet is a variety of eating apple with rough brownish skin.

clue.text: Link jam, surprisingly, with starter of unappealing spam

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters land in an unexpected order, so they are rearranged
the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A link stuck together with a tin of the unappetising luncheon meat, a strange kitchen picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges LINK, JAM and U (the 'starter of unappealing') together; 'spam' as tinned meat misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unwanted bulk email or advertising, the modern form of unsolicited post.

clue.text: Fish around lake, being at a loose end

indicators.note: around says the fish's name goes round the letter for lake

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An angler circling a lake with nothing much to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a loose end means having nothing to do, the same as being unoccupied.

clue.text: Dilapidated slum door, something beaten alone

indicators.note: dilapidated means falling apart, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A crumbling slum's door gets battered on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum solo is a passage where a drummer plays unaccompanied, hitting the drums by themselves.

clue.text: Second refusal by old college to provide game

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
no is a refusal
poly is short for polytechnic, a type of British college largely converted to universities in 1992

explanation.surface: A second turn-down from a former college to stage some contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopoly is a board game of buying property, an example of a game.

clue.text: Yell, losing head, producing blade

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to roar is to yell loudly

explanation.surface: A shout cut short produces a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat part of an oar is called its blade, so the whole is named by its key part.

clue.text: Took heart from freebie given to European political party

parts.note: a perk is a benefit given free on top of pay
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A political party cheered by a free gift from a European.
explanation.definitionFit: To perk up is to become more cheerful, as is to take heart.

clue.text: People giving up, heading from our IQ test, confused

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the pooled letters are rearranged
heading from means the first letter of the word our is removed

explanation.surface: Muddled test-takers abandoning our intelligence exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading from' strips O from OUR to leave UR, which joins IQ and TEST to be 'confused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quitters are those who abandon something, in the sense of giving up.

clue.text: Gradually develop passion for climbing: very English!

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word goes upwards, read backwards

parts.note: love is a passion

explanation.surface: Someone builds a passion for mountaineering, a very English pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to change and grow slowly over time, like a species adapting.

clue.text: Go after sex appeal in heavenly body

indicators.note: after puts the word for go behind the letters for sex appeal

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone takes their turn after a person with plenty of allure, all wrapped in a pun on a stunning body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly body' suggests an attractive figure, fitting 'sex appeal', but it means a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the ringed sixth planet from the sun, an astronomical object.

clue.text: Right about America's corrosive influence

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the letters for right go round the letters for America

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for America; the 's here means 'is'

explanation.surface: A political claim that the right wing is eating away at America.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust is the oxidation that eats into iron, so figuratively any decay that corrodes.

clue.text: Fruit revealed by lifting nail gun

indicators.note: lifting says the hidden letters are read backwards
revealed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit pops into view when someone picks up a nail gun.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'lifting' reads upwards, so ILGU, 'revealed by' nail gun, turns into the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine with wrinkled skin.

clue.text: Fleeing from concoction of methanol

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of methanol are mixed up

explanation.surface: Running away from a toxic brew of wood alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: On the lam is American slang for escaping from the police, running from capture.

clue.text: Heads for America — Palm Springs — enjoying recess

indicators.note: heads are the first letters, so each following word gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker sets off for Palm Springs in America to enjoy a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' as a holiday fits the surface, but it is the alcove in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: My French diary recalled an Asian nomad

parts.note: mon is French for my

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for diary is read backwards

parts.note: a log is a diary or record of events

explanation.surface: Someone remembers an entry in their French journal about meeting a wanderer of the steppes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mongol is a native of Mongolia, whose people have long herded animals on the move.

clue.text: Upright, not upper class, old expert musician

indicators.note: not says the letter for upper class is left out

parts.note: virtuous means morally upright
U is the abbreviation for upper class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A description of an honest, unpretentious, elderly master player.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a performer of outstanding technical skill, especially in music.

clue.text: Flesh mostly to freeze in tight corset

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: flesh is the physical body
to ice something is to freeze it

explanation.surface: Someone shivering in a tight corset, their flesh almost frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a dress, once worn laced like a corset.
